scope: Eighth-order observation-process audit of the unchanged EdgeBench v1 paper, public SForge implementation and all 51 public task contracts. OBS1/E48 is a Frontier-Science protocol proposal, not an EdgeBench treatment or performance result.
source_facts: The paper describes host-side auto-evaluation at fixed intervals and the official public configurations set eval_interval to 1800 seconds.

For non-game tasks, SForge _auto_eval_loop waits eval_interval, captures the live workspace, asynchronously submits it, then begins the next wait; the implementation does not retain a planned absolute-grid scheduled_at field.
For game_mode tasks, run_agent skips host auto-evaluation and scores agent-driven game sessions through the game API.

All 51 public contracts were scanned: 3 are game_mode=true and all three are text adventures; the public Interactive Games & Simulators family contains 8 tasks, of which the other 5 use artifact mode.
Archived public game step records contain move, action, observation, score, peak_score, max_score and done, but no wall-clock timestamp.

Ordinary evaluation reports retain a submitted_at time created inside judge_submission; the summarized in-memory history drops this field, and capture time, judge start/completion and underlying artifact edit time are distinct.

sle_experiment.design: Replay identical sentinel-complete immutable artifact/event trajectories under dense-event, fixed 5/15/30/60-minute, preregistered seeded-random-phase and agent-event-only observation kernels. Preserve scheduled capture, actual capture, artifact or state creation, judge start/completion and feedback-read times. Analyze material event times as interval-censored when dense replay is impossible. Separately retain timestamped actions, sensor readings and world transitions for path-dependent live-state laboratories.

distinct_from.S4: intervenes on when feedback is released to the agent
distinct_from.I1: intervenes on whether the observation process changes agent behavior or resource availability
distinct_from.M2: audits longitudinal run membership and best-so-far selector invariants

claim_boundary: The mode census and source semantics do not establish how EdgeBench internally constructed every published trajectory or whether observation heterogeneity changed any reported score, rank or fit.
The approximately 38000-hour raw trajectory corpus and figure-analysis code are not public, so OBS1 cannot be run on the EdgeBench headline data from the public release.
A nominal 1800-second eval_interval is not evidence of exact absolute-grid captures; source code shows a wait-capture-submit loop, but runtime scheduling and judge queues are unobserved here.
Game-mode tasks are not intrinsically invalid or inferior; they require a live-state measurement estimand rather than silent equivalence to replayable artifact snapshots.
OBS1/E48 was unrun when this source-audit artifact was frozen. Any later Frontier-Science replay report is separate evidence and cannot retroactively become an EdgeBench result.
